headline: 3D and connectomic spatial atlases resolve cell-cell organization in tissues
label: Spatial Omics Quantitative Inference Methods
summary: Preprints and a published method extend spatial single-cell atlases to perturbation, lineage benchmarking, and 3D reconstruction.
synthesis: The dominant thread is the move from isolated spatial measurements to integrated, quantitative reference structures. The rat post-pneumonectomy lung study pairs scRNAseq with Xenium spatial profiling and NICHES connectomics to model how cell-cell communication shifts after perturbation, and is presented as a generalizable spatial connectomic framework. The human heart organoid study integrates 16 single-cell RNA datasets from diverse differentiation protocols into one reference atlas, benchmarking maturation and lineage fidelity across protocols. Space-map addresses the third dimension, aligning serial tissue sections into 3D single-cell atlases from spatial transcriptomics and proteomics, with benchmarked accuracy. What is new across these items is the explicit benchmarking or generalizable framing of spatial and reference-level inference, rather than a single shared algorithm; the organoid and lung studies address different biological questions.
